overview.summary: A residue object preserving the sound-shape of a migration fleet losing coordination when the undersea spine fails faster than operators can reroute it.
overview.thesis: Interdependence became visible only when the cables stopped translating distance into certainty.
overview.viewer_hint: The media page should read as damaged evidence, not as an absent feature.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.body: The object captures the repeating impact pattern of power retries, ship pings, and synchronized distress after cable faults severed the route intelligence holding a migration fleet together.

sections.title: Infrastructure note
sections.body: Operators did not lose all channels at once. They lost enough precision that each remaining channel amplified uncertainty. Fleets continued moving inside a coordination architecture that had already become fiction.

sections.title: Recovered excerpt
sections.body: What remains is not speech but a repeating impact pattern from power retries, vessel pings, and a final burst of synchronized distress before every channel degrades into ocean noise.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.body: Residue records do not need full transcripts to be legible. Here the archive uses pattern recurrence to show a species that depended on invisible infrastructure more than it understood the cost of keeping it alive.
